snippet.title: What If YOU Had to Stop an Asteroid? ☄️
snippet.description:
An asteroid is heading for Earth, and you're the genius in charge. Nuke it? Rockets? Paint it white? 🙃 Plan A through D all fail… until you realize the real trick isn't pushing harder. It's pushing earlier. And NASA actually did it.

FACT CHECK
• NASA's DART mission (Sept 2022) crashed a small spacecraft into the asteroid moonlet Dimorphos and shortened its orbit around Didymos by about 32 minutes (from ~11 h 55 min to ~11 h 23 min). First real test of moving an asteroid on purpose.
• Blowing an asteroid apart can leave many fragments still on a collision course, which is why deflection is preferred over destruction.
• Yarkovsky effect: sunlight absorbed and re-emitted as heat gives an asteroid a tiny, steady push; changing how reflective its surface is (e.g. painting it) changes that push, but it acts over decades.
• Gravity tractor (Lu & Love, Nature, 2005): a spacecraft hovering next to an asteroid pulls it with its own gravity, a very gentle force that needs years to decades of warning.
• A change in speed of just a few centimeters per second, applied years in advance, adds up to thousands of kilometers by the time the asteroid reaches Earth.
